reviewMethod: Independent visual inspection of all eight original paper pages and scheme PDF pages 1–39, including every task, alternative method, graph, 49 marking components, attempt floor and special deduction. All 45 question and 45 complete solution crops visually inspected.
sourceNotes: All eight original pages and scheme pages 1–39 independently inspected, including the formula sheet and blank pages.
Q3(b), Q4(b) and the unnumbered Q7 graph retain their 3, 2 and 2 scoring components inside complete tasks.
Both tabular/direct graph evaluation and both compound-interest methods retain all original working and notes.
Required lists, paired roots and both inequalities are complete responses, not alternative routes.
The printed Q7 minimum −11.3 is within the published tolerance of the exact −11.5.
Q5(a) has a stray combined attempt heading of 3, but both named five-mark parts and their detailed notes consistently specify attempt 2.

cards.stem: Helen borrowed €4000 at 5·5% per annum compound interest. She paid back €1000 at the end of the first year.
cards.markingNote: The formula and yearly-interest approaches are alternative methods for the same 20 marks. Correct answers without work can imply earlier steps: €4220 earns 10 marks; €3220 earns 15; €3397·10 earns all 20. Select the full marks for the implied completed components.

cards.questionText: Solve the simultaneous equations 3x + 2y = 1 and 5x + 3y = 3.
cards.markingNote: Both variables are required. Correct answers without working earn 6 + 2 only; verification of both correct values in both equations earns 15 + 5. A randomly chosen first value followed by a calculated second value can earn the second five marks only.
